findings: Exposition (proof level, statement unaffected), 4°, l.605–607. The proof uses « Si V n'est pas l'intérieur d'un corps convexe, on peut trouver dans V une demi-droite L, c'est-à-dire une portion de droite limitée à deux points diamétralement opposés de la frontière de V ». It is stated without proof, and it is false for V = S(n). S(n) is an open convex part (Déf. 8) and not the interior of a convex body, and its frontier is empty, so no such portion of line exists (univ_not_demiDroite). In S(0) it contains no half-line at all. The fact holds exactly for the open convex parts other than S(n): an open convex part other than S(n) is strict (Sphere.isStrictConvexPart_of_isOpen), and the fact is proved for those (exists_demiDroite_of_ne_univ, exists_demiDroite), together with its converse (eq_interior_corpsConvexe_iff_not_demiDroite). The paper does not say why φ̃(V) ≠ S(n). It holds for every pocket: two antipodal points of φ̃(V) would be moved by one γ ∈ GS(n, R) into φ(P) ⊆ H̊ (neg_notMem_range_of_poche), the 1°b argument again.

Exposition (proof level, statement unaffected), 4°, l.609–612. The paper takes an arbitrary demi-droite L and moves one of its points into P by an automorphism g. The demi-droite can be taken through any point of V, because p + ℝx ⊆ F(V) for every p ∈ F(V) (demiDroite_of_not_salient). The proof here takes it through a point of φ(P), so this step needs no g. Prop. 7's corollary is still used, through 3°. The paper also leaves implicit the step « il résulte de la condition b … que gL est une demi-droite incluse dans H̊ ». It applies condition b to every sub-segment (gM, X) of gL, and these are segments of V because φ̃(V) is convex (3°). The formalisation makes this explicit: it builds each sub-segment as a segment of V from 3°'s strict convexity and the chart φ̃ (isProjSegment_of_chart).
questions: [sic] l.618 (transcription comment l.620; the scan, p. 255, prints « z(M) »): « gL est une droite … de cote constante égale à z(M) » is read « z(gM) ». M ∈ L is the point moved into P by g. Taken here: the constant cote of the line is that of its base point in φ(P), which is < 1 by IsPocheProj.cote_lt_one. A reading, not ruled.

OQ-71 (open, not decided here): is the component form of 1°'s second sentence the statement of record, or must the printed full form P = φ̃⁻¹(D ∩ φ̃(V)) be proved? Both assemblies are provided and neither is chosen. theoremeComposantePrinted gives 1° in component form with 2°–4°, proved in every dimension. theoremePrinted_iff states TheoremePrinted n ↔ ConnexePrinted n, so the printed Theorem is exactly the open connectedness. 2°–4° do not depend on the answer.

« demi-droite » (l.606) is read as Remarque 1's half-line of S(n), s({a x + b p | b > 0}) with x, p independent (Sphere.halfLine x p), whose two ends ±s(x) lie on the frontier of V. This is the paper's own gloss, « portion de droite limitée à deux points diamétralement opposés de la frontière de V ». Content-neutral.

« V n'est pas l'intérieur d'un corps convexe » (l.605) and 4°'s conclusion are read for φ̃(V) ⊆ S(n), the paper's convention φ̃ = id (l.593–594), as ¬ ∃ K, IsCorpsConvexeS n K ∧ range φ̃ = interior K (Déf. 11). Content-neutral.
3° « φ̃(V) est un convexe » is read as Déf. 8 in the ∪ reading (DEC-120). φ̃(V) is proved strict (theoreme_troisieme), so the conclusion also holds in the Minkowski reading. Content-neutral.

2° « simplement connexe » is read as Mathlib's SimplyConnectedSpace: nonempty, path connected, trivial fundamental groupoid. For P it is taken with the subspace topology. Content-neutral: P is a connected open set of a manifold.

kb_proposals: Convex geometry of open parts of S(n) (Chapter2/Theoreme.lean). Let C be an open strict convex part. If closure F(C) is salient, closure C is a convex body and C is its interior (isCorpsConvexeS_closure_of_salient). If ±x ∈ closure F(C), then p + ℝx ⊆ F(C) for EVERY p ∈ F(C) (demiDroite_of_not_salient), so a half-line can be placed through any chosen point. An open convex part other than S(n) is strict (Sphere.isStrictConvexPart_of_isOpen). interior (closure C) = C whenever C is open and F(C) is convex (interior_closure_eq_of_convex_F). Next user: T-bz-c2-theoreme-affine, 4° affine (« ne contient pas de droite »).

A loop moved by an automorphism g: use Mathlib's simply_connected_iff_loops_nullhomotopic and isSimplyConnected_iff_exists_homotopy_refl_forall_mem, then map the homotopy back with Path.Homotopic.map by g⁻¹. Close the base-point mismatch g⁻¹ • g • x = x with a subst lemma (path_homotopic_refl_of_eq), not with Path.cast.

The cote along a line of H̊ through m, with direction x ∈ ker l: take u := (Sphere.lbar l).smulRight ⟨x, hlx⟩ and v₀ := Sphere.nrep l m. Then Sphere.coe_smul_vadd gives ↑(t • u +ᵥ m) = s(v₀ + t x), and AffineMap.map_vadd gives z(t • u +ᵥ m) = t * z.linear u + z m. This is the template of Remarque 2's hsal (Poches.lean) and of 4° here.
Pitfall: after `apply MulAction.injective γ` the goal is a beta-redex `(fun x => γ • x) a = (fun x => γ • x) b`, and `rw [← hγ]` finds nothing. Run `show γ • a = γ • b` first.

If the full form is required, theoremePrinted_iff reduces the printed Theorem to ConnexePrinted, which is open, and the mark waits on a proof of ConnexePrinted alone. The row is unmarked per the dispatch (no ** in the docstring). OQ-45/OQ-61: 2°–4° call Prop. 7 and its corollary only (compact_dans_poche, deux_points_dans_poche; per T-bz-c2-compact AUDIT-1 these depend on neither OQ). They never call Prop. 4 or 6 directly, so the mark does not wait on OQ-45. Proofs follow the evidence's route with one simplification (findings 2): 4° places the demi-droite through a point of φ(P) instead of moving one in by g. Non-vacuity has two witnesses. First, the model ℝⁿ with the shell of cote 0 (P = V; theoreme_poche_balayable_model gives 1°–3°'s conclusions). Second, the half-line ]0, ∞[ with the strict shell P = ]0, 1[ ≠ V (theoreme_poche_balayable_demiDroite): every hypothesis of 2°–4° holds there, P is simply connected, and the conclusions hold, V simply connected, φ̃(V) convex and the interior of a convex body. demiDroite_hemisphere instantiates the demi-droite lemma's hypotheses (an open hemisphere of S(1)).
